import django
from django.conf import settings
settings.configure(INSTALLED_APPS=['django.contrib.contenttypes','django.contrib.auth'], DATABASES={}, USE_TZ=True, PASSWORD_HASHERS=['django.contrib.auth.hashers.PBKDF2PasswordHasher'])
django.setup()
from django.contrib.auth.forms import UserChangeForm, ReadOnlyPasswordHashField

# field defaults
f = ReadOnlyPasswordHashField()
assert f.disabled is True and f.required is False, (f.disabled, f.required)
print("ReadOnlyPasswordHashField: disabled=True, required=False by default")

# explicit override still possible
assert ReadOnlyPasswordHashField(disabled=False).disabled is False
print("explicit disabled=False still honored")

# UserChangeForm end-to-end: tampered POST must not change the hash
class F(UserChangeForm):
    class Meta(UserChangeForm.Meta):
        fields = ['username', 'password']
initial = {'username': 'test', 'password': 'pbkdf2_sha256$100000$a6Pucb1qSFcD$WmCkn9Hqidj48NVe5x0FEM6A9YiOqQcl/83m2Z5udm0='}
form = F(initial, initial=initial)
assert form.is_valid(), form.errors
assert form.cleaned_data['password'] == initial['password'], form.cleaned_data['password']
print("tampered POST keeps initial hash; clean_password no longer needed")

# rendered widget carries the disabled attribute
html = str(form['password'])
assert 'disabled' in html, html
print("renders with disabled attribute")
EOF
